The differential metabolite signature is anchored in **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (KEGG map00590 / SMP00075)**. All eight input metabolites map to this pathway with an FDR of 0.0 and a massive fold-enrichment (≈643×), driven by six matched compounds: arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid, and leukotriene A4.

**Key drivers and upstream/downstream relationships.** KEGG reaction-graph analysis confirms that arachidonic acid (C00219) is the biosynthetic precursor: it converts via an intermediate (C05356) to leukotriene A4 (C00909) and to 5-HETE (C04805) in two enzymatic hops, establishing arachidonic acid as the upstream driver. Leukotriene A4 is itself upstream of 5-HETE through the same intermediate, creating a directional cascade consistent with 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX) activation. Arachidonic acid is therefore the most upstream input compound, and its deviation plausibly propagates downstream to all measured eicosanoids.

**Biological significance.** Arachidonic acid sits at the branch point of the cyclooxygenase (COX) and lipoxygenase (LOX) pathways. A perturbation that increases free arachidonic acid while elevating both HETEs (5-HETE, 15-HETE) and leukotriene A4 points to a shift away from prostaglandin synthesis toward leukotriene-mediated signaling. The simultaneous presence of 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (a cyclopentenone prostaglandin with anti-inflammatory properties) and 5,6-epoxy-eicosatrienoic acid (an epoxy metabolite) suggests the treatment modulates both pro- and anti-inflammatory eicosanoid arms. This pattern is characteristic of selective COX-inhibition or polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation, where blocked prostaglandin production redirects the metabolic flux through the 5-LOX and 12/15-LOX routes. The resulting leukotriene and HETE elevation can amplify leukocyte chemotaxis, vascular permeability, and oxidative stress, linking the metabolomic changes to a defined inflammatory-resolution phenotype.
